And he went again to that high place opposite the city of Aswan,
from which the waters of the Nile burst forth and descend.
And he inspected it and saw
that the great rush of those waters could not be subjected to that which he had planned to do.
And thus he was ashamed,
and made an excuse to al-Hakim.
And when it was not accepted as it should have been,
he was very much afraid.
And he found no other means to escape from the malice of al-Hakim
except by showing that he had a demon and was mad.
And he feigned this so much
that they bound him with chains,
and put a seal upon everything that he possessed.
And he remained mad like this
until al-Hakim died;
then he returned to his senses.
And he sat quietly in one of the houses at the gate of the Great Mosque of Cairo,
and he began and wrote about seventy books on geometry.
And he also used to write three books every year:
the Almagest,
the Intermediate Books on the Spheres (or of the Sphere),
and Euclid;
and he used to sell them for one hundred and fifty Egyptian dinars.
And from this he lived,
until he died in the year four hundred and twenty of the Arabs [1029/1030 AD].
And in the year 414 [of the Greeks / AH 414],
he subdued most of the cities.
And when he penetrated into the country a journey of four months,
he reached a fortress whose name was Kawakir,
and in it was one of the kings of the Indians.
And when he waged a fierce war against him,
an Indian envoy came out to him,
sitting upon a couch,
carried by four men,
and he came to Mahmud.
And he said to him:
"My lord asks you:
'What kind of human being are you?'" And Mahmud answered:
"I am a Muslim man,
who calls those who deny God to the faith,
and I persecute those who worship idols.
And you Indians:
either you believe in our God, submit to our law, and eat the flesh of oxen,
or you give us as tribute every year a thousand elephants and a thousand manehs of gold."
And the envoy said:
"As for the flesh of oxen,
it is among the impossible things that we should eat it.
Yes, the faith of which you speak—
send to us... {OCR?}"
